name: clear_tables_and_unpack_rows
description: Zeroes a large block of longwords, then copies sixteen words from the source pointer into one table while clearing two companion tables. It then copies three groups of ten longwords from the source stream into a buffer and writes all-ones sentinel values after each group.

name: clear_palette_and_scratch_block
description: Writes zero to sixteen longwords in a RAM block and, in the same loop, to the matching sixteen longwords of the custom chip color register block, clearing both.

name: poll_until_expected_status
description: Calls a helper routine repeatedly and keeps looping until that helper returns the value sixty-two, then returns to the caller.

name: step_nibbles_toward_target
description: Compares the three four-bit fields of two sixteen-bit values and moves each differing field of the first value one step toward the second, incrementing or decrementing it by one unit.

name: set_channel_bit_mask
description: Takes the low six bits of the input byte and, when that value is below four, stores a single set bit at that position in a global mask variable. The code does not write any hardware register.

name: loop_helper_then_clear_flag
description: Calls a helper routine sixteen times in a row and then sets a global flag variable to zero.

name: initialize_record_from_helper
description: Sets a bit-mask global and ORs it into a flag word, clears three state bytes in a record, then calls a helper and stores its results into the record's position, length and pointer fields. A small count installs a callback address with a fixed value; a larger count stores a computed pointer instead.

name: enter_infinite_loop
description: Contains no work and spins forever, so control never returns to the caller.

name: copy_target_from_source
description: Reads a record pointer from its argument and, when the low bit of the input byte is set and the source value is nonzero, copies a longword and a word from the source record to the target pointed to by the record. It returns the input byte shifted right by one.

name: process_flagged_copy_sequence
description: When a global flag is set, it stores a helper result in a global, calls four helpers, then takes a returned byte and performs the same conditional longword and word copy as the other copy routine, returning that byte halved. When the flag is clear it returns zero.

name: decode_pattern_row_commands
description: Returns zero when the pattern pointer is null. Otherwise it advances a row counter and, at the end of a row, decodes each channel entry, applying effect-nibble commands for speed, volume, position jump and a high-nibble sub-command group, then writes results into per-channel records. It returns early on one end-marker command.

name: decode_pattern_row_variant
description: A near-identical twin of the pattern row decoder that keeps its per-row flag in a different byte. It decodes each channel entry with the same effect-nibble commands and writes results into per-channel records, returning early on one end-marker command.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Bad data: the decoded bytes are not a valid routine. They perform a few bit-set operations on records and then end in an invalid-instruction halt, so there is no meaningful behaviour to describe.

name: update_channel_state_and_dispatch
description: Loads a counter from a channel record and, when it is nonzero, decrements it and may update a level and a period word from a table. It then walks four channel records and finishes by calling through a handler table.

name: adjust_level_from_nibble
description: Adds the high nibble or subtracts the low nibble of the input byte from a channel level byte, clamped between zero and sixty-four. It stores the level and an optional period word, walks four channel entries and finishes with an indirect handler call.

name: set_level_from_nibbles
description: Sets a channel level byte to the input byte plus the high nibble of the second argument, clamped to at most sixty-four. It then stores an optional period word, walks four channel entries and finishes with an indirect handler call.

name: copy_level_and_dispatch_entries
description: Stores an optional period word and copies the channel level into a field, then walks four entries. It sets a bit-mask global when a counter expires, and finishes with an indirect handler call.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: store_global_address_pair
description: Writes the address of a global variable into a field of the record in the address register, then returns the longword read through the input pointer together with that pointer advanced by six bytes.

name: fill_global_buffer_from_table
description: When the table pointer is valid and its row count is nonzero, copies byte pairs from each table row into two interleaved positions of a global buffer, advancing by a row stride. Otherwise it zeroes a fixed run of words in that buffer.

name: return_status_from_helper_result
description: Calls a helper and, depending on whether it returned zero, calls one of two follow-up routines. It returns zero in the first case and minus one in the second.

name: call_optional_helper_then_step
description: If a global flag is nonzero, it calls one helper. It then unconditionally calls a second helper and returns.

name: select_record_and_set_state
description: Calls a helper, then, when the record pointer is valid, installs the record's handler address as the dispatch target. It sets or clears one bit of a global flag from a flag bit in the record, returns the record's word value, and stores the record's counter byte and a fixed count of two in state fields. The code does not read any hardware register.

name: call_pending_dispatch_if_flagged
description: When the global flag is nonzero, it clears the dispatch target and calls a helper, returning the byte that helper returns. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: clear_dispatch_slot_return_zero
description: Clears the dispatch target slot to zero and returns zero.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: read_and_clear_global_flag
description: Returns the current value of a global flag byte and resets that flag to zero if it was nonzero.

name: add_to_pointer_if_nonzero
description: Adds the second input value to the longword at the input pointer, but only when that longword is nonzero, and stores the sum back through the pointer.

name: rebase_offset_tables_and_finish
description: Calls four helpers, then calls a helper repeatedly until it returns zero. For each block whose negative-flagged header field is set, it adds the block's own base address to every longword in that block. It then calls a helper until zero and returns the result of a final helper only when a record field is nonzero, otherwise zero.

name: copy_sequence_setup_into_record
description: Writes fixed values into a record, including a maximum-value field, a mode word and a flag, and calls a helper. It copies one longword and three words from the pointer that helper provides into the record, sets the mode word to a new value, then calls a second helper and stores a fixed pointer and a small count. A global is set to twenty-three when the input count is two.

name: initialize_four_record_blocks
description: Calls a helper, then writes the same fixed pointer, a count of three and a value of five hundred eight into four fixed-offset blocks of one record.

name: return_register_pair_after_call
description: Calls a helper and then returns the two register values it was given as one eight-byte result, passing them through unchanged.

name: enter_infinite_loop
description: Performs no work and spins forever, so control never returns to the caller. The decompiled body touches no register.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: set_global_to_sixteen
description: Stores the value sixteen into a global variable and returns.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: call_helper_with_control_words
description: Stores a computed offset and the address of a global, writes a fixed control word to that global, and calls a helper. It then writes a second control value and calls the helper again. The referenced text is a disk file path, but the code shows no read of that file itself.

name: unresolved_single_instruction_routine
description: The decompiler produced no output for this one-instruction routine, so its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence. Only its single caller is known.

name: set_fixed_base_constant
description: Stores a fixed constant equal to twelve mebibytes into a global longword variable and returns.

description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: clear_block_then_dispatch_calls
description: Clears a sixteen-word block in a global area, then calls an entry from a function table. Depending on whether that call returned zero, it calls one of two other table entries, and it finishes with a final table call.

name: call_table_with_buffer_length
description: Calls a function-table entry with the address of a global buffer and a length of 3840 bytes, then calls a second table entry. It returns the first call's result paired with the input register value.

name: call_table_then_trap
description: Calls a function-table entry and a second routine, stores the value 4096 in a global, and invokes a trap with vector zero. The trailing invalid-instruction halt is a decompiler artefact, not a behaviour.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Bad data: the body decodes to nothing but an invalid-instruction halt, so there is no routine behaviour to describe.

name: conditional_table_call_with_constant
description: Calls a function-table entry and, when its result is nonzero, calls another table entry with a fixed constant, then calls a helper. It returns the input register pair unchanged.

name: call_table_entry_above_two
description: Calls two helpers and a table entry only when the global value exceeds two, then ends in an invalid-instruction halt. The halt is a decompiler artefact, so the behaviour is just that conditional call sequence.

name: xor_countdown_scramble_block
description: Walks eighty bytes from the input pointer, XOR-ing each byte with a counter that counts down from eighty, and returns eighty.

name: call_table_with_fixed_address
description: Calls a function-table entry with a fixed high-range constant and two zero arguments. It returns a zero word together with the register value from its input.

name: store_fixed_constant_through_pointer
description: Writes the fixed constant 524288 into the longword pointed to by the input address and returns.

name: call_table_entry_return_pair
description: Calls a function-table entry and returns the two input register values unchanged as one eight-byte result.

name: unpack_backward_packed_stream
description: Repeats until the destination pointer reaches the start of its range. When a flag byte from a helper is zero it reads a count and writes that many copies of a byte read from the helper, moving backward through the destination. Otherwise it reads a length and offset and copies a run of bytes from an earlier position back into the destination.

name: decrement_byte_with_space_wrap
description: Loops for a count taken from the input word minus one, decrementing a byte register each iteration and replacing an underflowing zero with a space character. It makes no memory accesses or calls.

name: increment_indexed_word_return_byte
description: Adds two to a sixteen-bit field at an offset formed from the index register and the input base address, then returns the input byte unchanged.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: set_global_masked_bits_value
description: Stores a fixed value in a global, then replaces it with a masked form of that value that keeps only the top two bits of the byte and sets bit three.

name: store_fixed_pointer_table_entries
description: Writes five fixed longword constants into consecutive slots of a global table. The code does nothing else.

name: clear_stored_block_or_cycle
description: If a stored pointer is set and the requested size fits, it zeroes that many bytes, advances the pointer and calls a helper. Otherwise it loops over every sixteen-bit count, writing a masked value into a global.

name: initialize_indexed_table_entry
description: For an index below two hundred fifty-five, it writes fixed words into an indexed table entry spaced sixty bytes apart. It stores the low and high halves of an address in that entry and writes a derived index value and a pointer through the input pointer.

name: initialize_indexed_table_entry
description: For an index below two hundred fifty-five, it writes fixed words into an indexed table entry spaced sixty bytes apart. It stores the low and high halves of an address in that entry and writes a derived index value and a pointer through the input pointer.

name: set_three_entry_words
description: Writes the same fixed value, five hundred ten, into three words of an indexed table entry spaced sixty bytes apart.

name: fill_column_across_table_entries
description: Writes the input word into one fixed field of each of 256 consecutive table entries spaced sixty bytes apart.

name: set_initial_global_state
description: Assigns a long run of fixed and computed constants to global variables and a few RAM slots, and calls two helpers during setup. The visible pseudo-code does not show what the values control.

name: multiply_and_call_helper
description: Stores the product of two 16-bit inputs in a global, sets it to one, and calls a helper. It clears the global when a flag is set, then ends in an invalid-instruction halt, which is a decompiler artefact.

name: compute_scaled_flag_and_call
description: Sets a global to two, or to a fixed constant when a flag is nonzero, and multiplies it by the flag value. It then calls a helper, clears the global when a flag is set, and calls a second helper when the global is nonzero. The trailing invalid-instruction halt is a decompiler artefact.

name: store_input_and_call_helper
description: Stores the input word in a global, sets a global to one, and calls a helper. It clears the global when a flag is set and calls a second helper when the global is nonzero. The trailing invalid-instruction halt is a decompiler artefact.

name: call_helpers_then_trap
description: Stores the input word in a global and calls helpers, then clears or sets several global and RAM slots according to the low bits the helper returns. It stores a fixed constant, calls a helper and invokes trap vector zero before an invalid-instruction halt.

name: check_status_then_trap
description: Calls a helper, then clears or sets globals depending on its returned bits and a zero flag. It stores a fixed constant, calls a helper and invokes trap vector zero before an invalid-instruction halt.

name: set_status_then_trap
description: Clears or sets globals based on a status byte, stores a fixed constant, calls a helper and invokes trap vector zero before an invalid-instruction halt.

name: stub_no_function_body
description: The decompiler produced no function body for this entry, so there is no visible behaviour to describe.

name: set_flag_on_match_trap
description: Sets a global to one when the input byte equals a fixed negative value, clears two fields, stores a fixed constant, calls a helper and invokes trap vector zero before an invalid-instruction halt.

name: call_helper_then_trap
description: Calls a helper, invokes trap vector zero, clears a global, then ends in an invalid-instruction halt. The halt is a decompiler artefact.

name: initialize_display_and_interrupts
description: Sets up a block of global variables from a stored address, selects a buffer address and calls several helpers to initialize state. Its facts list bitplane, beam and interrupt control registers, and the pseudo-code in the source is truncated before the full sequence is shown.

name: compute_status_then_call_helpers
description: Updates a few globals with fixed arithmetic, calls helpers depending on the results, and ends by storing the value sixteen in a global.

name: wait_flag_then_init_record
description: Spins forever when a global is nonzero. Otherwise it polls a global bit until it clears, calls a helper, stores a fixed address and a zero word into a record, and sets a global to all ones.

name: expand_nibble_fields_into_tables
description: Copies thirty-two words from a source table, then for each word splits its nibble fields into three longword tables. It stores the fields as scaled values and differences shifted right by five, and calls several helpers.

name: sum_nibble_tables_packed
description: If the global counter exceeds thirty-one, it copies thirty-two words from a table into a target and clears a global. Otherwise it adds pairs of longwords from six tables across thirty-two entries, clamps each low nibble of the sums to fifteen, and packs three nibbles into one word stored in a table. Each call increments the global counter.

description: Copies thirty-two words from a source table into a target table, zeroing each source word as it goes. It then calls helpers, stores a fixed address and a zero word into a record, and loops until a global becomes zero.

name: program_entry_calls_bit_reader
description: Program entry point whose decompiled body timed out, so only its facts are known. It calls a bit-reader refill routine and a multi-bit read routine, and it writes the COLOR00 colour register.

name: configure_blitter_and_copper
description: Decompiled body unavailable, so only its facts are known. It touches the blitter registers, the copper list pointer, DMA and interrupt control registers and the controller port registers, and calls six other routines.

name: copy_copper_and_dma_settings
description: Copies a longword into the copper pointer register, then writes a word into the DMA control register and a word into the interrupt enable register from fixed source fields. It returns a longword read through a pointer.

name: copy_string_until_marker_pattern
description: Copies bytes from the input string into a global buffer until it reaches an 'A' whose byte two places later is 'M'. It then null-terminates the buffer and calls a helper.

name: hash_uppercased_string_lookup
description: Clears a block of 544 longwords and calls helpers. When a status flag is clear and a stored count equals two, it converts the characters of a string to uppercase in place and computes a hash modulo seventy-two to select a table entry, then compares the string with that entry. The source pseudo-code is truncated after this point.

name: match_pattern_then_copy_run
description: Matches input bytes against a stored sequence using a case-folding mask and calls helpers when it matches. It then scales a helper result by eleven, copies a run of characters into a buffer, and returns a pair of values. The source pseudo-code is truncated.

name: emit_longword_bytes_rotating
description: Writes the bytes of a longword out one at a time, rotating it left by eight bits each step, up to a stored end pointer. It then scales a helper result by eleven, loops while calling helpers, and returns a pair of values. The source pseudo-code is truncated.

name: call_helper_adjust_result_pair
description: Calls a helper and, if it returns nonzero, subtracts a stacked argument from the result and calls a second helper. It returns the result paired with the stacked value.

name: call_helper_adjust_result_pair
description: Calls a helper and, if it returns nonzero, subtracts a stacked argument from the result and calls a second helper. It returns the result paired with the stacked value.

name: wait_field_then_clear_longs
description: Counts down from a large fixed iteration count while a record's halfword field is zero, returning if the count expires. Once the field is nonzero, it clears four longwords through the record's pointers.

name: poll_helper_until_nonzero_status
description: Loops while a helper's result is zero or a flag is clear, calling two helpers on each pass, and returns when that condition is met.

name: decrement_global_counter
description: Decrements a global counter by one and returns.

name: read_longword_block_until_zero
description: Calls helpers and, while a condition holds, fills a buffer of 128 longwords from a helper's returned values. It stops filling early when a returned value is zero and repeats until its loop flag clears.

name: divide_input_by_eleven
description: Sets a global counter to five and returns the input word divided by eleven.

name: wait_while_status_bit_set
description: Calls two helpers, then calls a helper repeatedly while bit four of a status byte in the record is set.

name: write_byte_set_port_bit
description: Calls a helper, writes a fixed byte and then the input byte through the record pointer, and sets bit two of a CIA port register.

name: set_cia_port_bit_two
description: Sets bit two of a CIA port register and returns.

name: clear_bit_wait_on_status
description: Clears one bit selected by a helper's result from a record byte and calls two helpers. If a status bit is set, it writes the seven low bits of a value and then waits on another status bit for a bounded count.

name: set_control_bits_busy_wait
description: Clears bit one and sets bit zero of a control byte, then runs a busy-wait over a register read sixty-four times. The loop condition appears in simplified form in the pseudo-code.

name: set_control_bit_busy_wait
description: Sets bit one, clears bit zero and then sets bit zero of a control byte, then runs a busy-wait over a register read sixty-four times. The loop condition appears in simplified form in the pseudo-code.

name: scan_sync_words_clear_blocks
description: Repeatedly compares a seven-bit field with a counter and calls helpers. It clears blocks of longwords, sets a pointer pair and a control word, and scans words for a fixed sync value under a bounded timeout, calling helpers between passes.

name: step_counter_then_scan_sync
description: Steps a byte counter toward a target value while calling helpers, then clears blocks of longwords and scans words for a fixed sync value under a bounded timeout. It returns early on a helper's failure result.

name: scan_sync_words_stepwise_compare
description: Steps a seven-bit value toward a target by one per helper call, then clears blocks and scans words for a fixed sync value under a bounded timeout. It returns early on a helper's failure result.

name: scan_sync_words_fill_blocks
description: Clears blocks of longwords, sets a pointer pair and a control word, and scans words for a fixed sync value under a bounded timeout. It then steps a byte value toward a target and calls helpers between passes.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one helper and returns to its caller.

name: depack_pp20_stream_backward
description: Returns unless the input begins with the four-character signature PP20. Otherwise it copies a header block of 128 longwords, reads a packed length from the end of the input, and decodes packed bit fields backward into the destination, calling helpers for each bit read.

name: call_helper_when_shifted_zero
description: Shifts a longword right by a count taken from a register and calls a helper only when the shifted value is zero. Otherwise it returns.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one helper and returns to its caller.

name: shift_out_bits_with_refill
description: Loops over a count taken from the input word, shifting one bit at a time out of a bit buffer and accumulating the shifted bits into a result. It calls a helper to refill the buffer whenever it empties.

name: shift_bits_until_counter_expires
description: Shifts a bit buffer repeatedly and calls a helper to refill it whenever it empties, returning when the counter reaches minus one.

name: unpack_backward_packed_runs
description: Copies bytes backward from a source into the destination, using a count from a helper. When a helper value equals a marker it reads a second count and fills backward with a byte from a helper, stopping when the destination pointer reaches the start of its range.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Does nothing and returns immediately to its caller.

name: unpack_backward_packed_runs_alt
description: Copies runs backward from a source into the destination, using a stored offset and a count from a helper. When the helper value equals a marker it reads a repeat count and fills backward with a helper byte.

name: undecompiled_single_instruction_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: one instruction, referenced by address and called by two routines. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: undecompiled_routine_with_two_calls
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: fifty-three instructions, referenced by address and calling two other routines. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: undecompiled_routine_with_one_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: fourteen instructions, referenced by address and calling one other routine. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: set_global_to_thirty_two
description: Sets a global variable to thirty-two and returns.

name: undecompiled_long_routine_one_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: forty-nine instructions, referenced by address and calling one other routine. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: undecompiled_routine_with_one_call
description: The decompiler timed out, so only facts are known: fourteen instructions, referenced by address and calling one other routine. Its behaviour cannot be determined from the evidence.

name: copy_sixteen_byte_groups_fixed
description: Copies consecutive groups of four longwords from one fixed address to another, repeating for a fixed count of groups.

name: copy_sixteen_byte_groups_fixed
description: Copies consecutive groups of four longwords from one fixed source address into a fixed destination, repeating for a fixed count of groups.

name: render_text_glyphs_into_buffer
description: Renders each character of an input string as an eight-row glyph taken from a font table indexed from the space character, writing the rows at a fixed stride into an image buffer. A newline moves the output to the next line position.

name: init_four_audio_channel_registers
description: Writes the same pointer value and a length of four into the four audio channel register blocks and clears their period fields. It also sets a global, derives a pointer chain from data tables, and stores values in RAM slots.

name: init_audio_channels_and_dma
description: Performs the same audio channel register setup as its neighbour, then writes DMA and interrupt control values and calls a helper. The pseudo-code is truncated in the source.

name: reset_record_fields_to_defaults
description: Initialises a record by storing a value from the input and one from a second record, setting a byte to sixty-three, and zeroing a series of fields at fixed offsets.

name: clear_global_status_bit
description: Sets a global to fifteen, then to seven hundred eighty, then clears bit one of it.

name: clear_low_byte_cycle_counter
description: Clears the low byte of a global word and decrements a counter byte, reloading it from a limit when it goes negative. It calls four helpers and then copies the global word back out.

name: advance_channel_data_pointer
description: Advances a channel's data pointer through a table, reads a length and a period from table values, and updates the channel's volume and pointer fields. It calls helpers when a step counter is reached. The pseudo-code is truncated in the source.

name: step_channel_period_with_sign
description: Advances a six-bit position and, when its record allows, looks up a table entry to set a period and pointer. It applies a delta with a sign flag, counts a step value, and toggles a direction value.

name: step_channel_period_set_flag
description: Performs the same channel period step as its neighbour with table lookup and sign-flag update. It also sets or clears bit one of a global depending on the input byte.

name: step_channel_period_negated_seed
description: Stores the negated input word in a record field, then performs the same channel period step with table lookup and sign-flag update as its neighbour.

name: step_channel_scaled_offset
description: Stores a scaled input value plus a base into a record field, advances a six-bit position, and when its record allows, looks up a table entry to set a period and pointer. It applies a sign-flag delta and steps a counter. The pseudo-code is partial.

name: step_channel_period_long_variant

name: step_colour_nibbles_to_targets

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0C70
name: write_colour_nibbles_row_entries
description: Writes packed four-bit colour values for a row of entries, stepping fields toward targets and waiting on a band-limited list value before each write. It calls helpers and returns when the row counter expires.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0C8E
name: step_colour_nibbles_hi_field
description: Steps the high-nibble fields of a stored colour toward their targets for each entry, waiting on a band-limited list value before each write. It calls helpers and returns when the row counter expires.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0CAC
name: step_colour_nibbles_row_variant
description: Steps the four-bit colour fields toward targets for each row entry, waiting on a band-limited list value before each write. It stores a combined value into the list and calls helpers between rows.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0CBA
name: step_colour_nibbles_row_loop
description: Loops over rows, stepping each four-bit colour field toward its target and writing the packed result into the list. It waits on a band-limited list value before each entry and calls helpers between rows.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0CD0
name: decrement_colour_nibbles_to_zero
description: Repeats sixteen rows, waiting until a list value falls within a fixed band, then decrements each four-bit colour field toward zero and writes it back. It calls helpers between rows.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:JStrike:0:0D22
name: decrement_colour_nibbles_loop
description: Calls helpers and then, while entries remain, decrements each four-bit colour field toward zero and writes the packed result into the list. It waits on a band-limited list value before each entry.

description: Program entry point. name: build_chunk_pointer_table
description: Scans a byte table for successive values and, for each value, fills thirty pointer slots with buffer chunk addresses spaced by a per-entry offset. It then sets several status globals.

description: Selects a value from a global table using a counter taken modulo three and a nibble of a record byte, and stores it in a record field. It returns the masked control word.

name: copy_word_field_between_records
description: Copies a sixteen-bit field from one record offset into another offset in a second record, then returns.

description: Scans a row of a global table for the first entry not above a masked input value, falling back to a fixed entry when none qualifies. It stores the chosen value in a record field and sets a flag byte when that value is below the record's target.

key: jungle strike (1994)(ocean)[cr trader's dream][t +6 freezers](disk 1 of 3)/Jungle Strike (1994)(Ocean)[cr Trader's Dream][t +6 Freezers](Disk 1 of 3).adf:Frs.exe:0:11FA
